text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bahraini press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A fire which gutted a house in Mosalla on August 12 killing two people was not deliberate, a government official says.
- Arab Insurance Group to increase its capital before the end of the year. The Bahrain-based group plans to offer shares worth $180 million to private investors.
- Families in Bahrain are to be offered the chance to buy government-built flats for the first time at a low cost of between 17,000-21,000 dinars.
- Bahrain International Bank makes a $10.1 million net income in the first six months of 1997, up 12 percent from the same period a year earlier.

- The Bahraini Saudi Aluminium Marketing Company (Balco) has signed agreements to sell 482,000 tonnes of aluminium, its general manager says. Balco sells aluminium produced by Aluminium Bahrain, the Middle East's biggest producer.
- Emir Sheikh Isa wishes Qatar's Emir early recovery from a surgery he underwent in the United States.
- Prime minister praises relationship between Bahrain and Egypt during a cabinet meeting on Sunday.
- Percentage of Bahrainis working in the government sector stands at 95 percent, an official says.
